searchText: <mikeneuder> i see the call on the calendar, does that generate a zoom link ? <mikeneuder> im prepping for mostly a whiteboard session <potuz0> Shit that's today? <potuz0> What time? <tbenr> in 53min <mikeneuder> https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/82900938377?pwd=bXjtGLWgDr9nSPavVvzNnbzabNKAp3.1 ouch <mikeneuder> lol ok bye <terencechain> bear market vibe <mikeneuder> was that matt ? <terencechain> free account? <tbenr> i guess lightclient was the owner of everithing If we would have a merkle proof of account in IL summary then I can verify it and then the only thing to trust is I need to check grandparents state root, which I can even if I don't have it's state as it's in block header Thus making block validation not dependent on grandparents state Copying here, I think it's fine to leave the summary in ACD Here's my take from the call - Some of us (I think most but Marius and perhaps Lukasz) think that we have a solution for validity - Some also think that we have a solution for availability if we deal with either RPC requests for head split views or commit summaries to the block. - There's a proposal from Enrico to work with the proposed solution for validity and disregard for the time being about availability - There's an idea of Lukasz to use any state change in the account in the parent state to consider that for satisfaction of the IL summary entry. - Homework for EL devs: either convince yourselves that the solution for validity works or convince us that it doesn't. Did I miss anything? <mikeneuder> lgtm!! <@543900561460822016> For the future, I am curious about your statement about account abstraction in general. I know I asked you before and failed but I'd like to have a chat for you to explain me the generalized validity conditions. Will this general AA forbid account inclusion or wuold it make it revert? So per my understanding, if the EL state transition stores in the post state the list of accounts "touched" in any ways during the state transition, then it is always possible to verify the summary of the next block, no matter the type of the transaction. Correct? I guess the evil is in "touched". Marius said that they all keep and have access to the parent state, so I consider this problem theoretical only unless someone corrects me I think for validity we can assume that the EL has all the info int he parent state as they want and we can specify it as such perhaps although a builder could easily add a tx that "touches" accounts avoiding including censoring tx (so would do a cost analysis of doing that vs profit from block) but it also a way to get out of jam when IL isn't available and builder wants to build block and has a summary ye, "touch" seems like a weak condition I captured the IL call notes #3 here: https://hackmd.io/@ttsao/ryCG0cTJA <mikeneuder> tyty!! In the general case it would forbid inclusion (much the same as a tx cannot be included when the balance cannot afford it) Has this been specified in some of these EIPs so that I can take a look? At some point we either come up with some way of dealing with this abstraction or we start constraining AA designs, but this seems like a fundamental problem down the line maybe check this out https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/blob/master/RIPS/rip-7560.md Thanks! will look into this There are three invariants that I can see - Current one: a transaction can only be invalidated by sending from the same address - Current 3074: a transaction can only be invalidated by changing the state of the account that sent it (for example spending balances) - More abstract version: a transaction can be invalidated by any change in the execution state pertaining any storage slot of any contract. Seems like the third one destroys completely any hopes for our designs. We could in principle require that AA designers include enough annotations in their transactions as to make them compatible with ILs, but this quickly seems to devolve. Given Ansgar's comments before I tend to think that we should aim to solve up to the current 3074 status and no more native AA requires so many changes that I really don't think we should try to solve ILs for it today maybe so, but i do think it means we need to be pretty confident that ILs are necessary today. otherwise we risk making a change that isn't strictly required *and* is not compatible with some farther future thoughts on accounts

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Here's my take from the call
- Some of us (I think most but Marius and perhaps Lukasz) think that we have a solution for validity
- Some also think that we have a solution for availability if we deal with either RPC requests for head split views or commit summaries to the block. 
- There's a proposal from Enrico to work with the proposed solution for validity and disregard for the time being about availability 
- There's an idea of Lukasz to use any state change in the account in the parent state to consider that for satisfaction of the IL summary entry. 
- Homework for EL devs: either convince yourselves that the solution for validity works or convince us that it doesn't. 
Did I miss anything?
